  Where research by Youssef Benzarti on VAT pass-through has entered policy debates in
  Denmark, Japan, the UK, Austria, Spain, Greece, France and across Europe, and press
  coverage of it.
---

Eight debates over cutting VAT, most recent first.

### Denmark, 2026 — the food VAT proposal

Denmark is preparing to abolish VAT on fruit and vegetables and halve it on the rest of the food
basket, at a cost now put at 17.4 billion kroner a year. Whether a cut that size reaches shelf
prices is what the Finance Committee asked the Ministry of Finance in June.

**[My memo to the Committee](memo.pdf)** answers from the European evidence: what pass-through
looks like once the estimates are restricted to food, and to the kind of rate change Denmark is
actually proposing, and what the studies the Ministry assembled do and do not establish.

[Jyllands-Posten](https://jyllands-posten.dk/politik/ECE19394802/) interviewed me in June 2026;
[TV 2](https://nyheder.tv2.dk/politik/2026-06-19-forsker-piller-centralt-regeringsforslag-fra-hinanden)
followed on 19 June.

### Japan, 2026–27 — the food consumption-tax cut

Japan will cut the consumption tax on food from 8 percent to 1 percent for two years from April
2027. I set out the case against in an interview with
[Nikkei](https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUA050C00V00C26A7000000/) on 7 July 2026 —
「一時的な減税、終了後に物価高騰リスク　消費税にフィンランドの教訓」, temporary cuts risk higher
prices once they end — drawing on the Finnish hairdressing experiment and on the Argentine
evidence that monitoring holds increases down when a rate is restored.

The numbers were already in the government's own record. The [Cabinet Secretariat working
group](https://www.cas.go.jp/jp/seisaku/kokuminkaigi/contents/20260424/minutes.pdf) that
considered the cut minuted pass-through of 13 percent on reductions against 55 percent on
increases, averaged over every EU VAT change between 1996 and 2015, together with the Argentine
finding that prices ended above where they started once the tax came back, except where the
increases were policed.

### United Kingdom, 2026 — the hospitality VAT cut

Britain weighed a £12bn VAT cut for hospitality.
[Tax Policy Associates](https://taxpolicy.org.uk/2026/06/12/hospitality-vat-cut-who-benefits/)
asked in June 2026 who would actually gain, and answered it partly from our work.

### Austria, 2026 — the food VAT cut

Austria cut VAT on staple foods from 10 percent to 4.9 percent on 1 July 2026. Two months
earlier, Parliament's [Budgetdienst](https://www.parlament.gv.at/fachinfos/budgetdienst/Senkung-der-Umsatzsteuer-auf-ausgewaehlte-Nahrungsmittel)
built the asymmetry between increases and decreases into its analysis of the measure.

### Spain, 2023 — the basic-foods VAT cut

Spain's leading economics blog, [Nada es
Gratis](https://nadaesgratis.es/miguel-almunia/los-efectos-de-la-reduccion-del-iva-de-los-alimentos-basicos),
judged the cut in March 2023 against our Argentina study: 85 percent pass-through in the large
chains, 35 percent in small shops. The European Commission's Joint Research Centre assessed the
same reform in *Price Effects of Temporary VAT Rate Cuts: Evidence from Spanish Supermarkets*.

### Greece, 2026 — a food VAT cut declined

Greece chose a voluntary supplier price agreement instead of cutting the rate. The small-business
institute IME GSEVEE reviewed the evidence first, in [Informational Brief
37](https://imegsevee.gr/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/ioannidis_fpa_2026.pdf) of June 2026, drawing
on three of our papers among 32 studies covering 69 VAT episodes. It reads the recent episodes
differently than we do: it finds cuts in 2022 and 2023 passing through almost fully, and more
fully than increases.

### Europe, 2020 — VAT cuts as pandemic stimulus

Germany cut VAT for six months from July 2020, Britain cut it for hospitality, and Rome floated a
cut of its own. Whether any of it would reach shelf prices was fought over while the policies were
being written. [Bloomberg
Opinion](https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2020-06-26/vat-cuts-are-a-bad-idea-for-germany-britain-and-italy)
made the case against on 26 June; [Il Sole 24
Ore](https://www.econopoly.ilsole24ore.com/2020/06/30/taglio-iva/) followed four days later,
asking whether a cut supports demand or firms.

### France, 2018 — the reduced rates under review

In May 2018 the Institut des politiques publiques published our evaluation of the 2009 restaurant
VAT cut, then one of the largest business subsidies in France at around €3bn a year. The press ran
it for four days. Ten days after it appeared, the Finance Minister said he would not rule out
re-examining the reduced rates on restaurants, housing and transport, and the story turned from
what the 2009 cut had done to which rates might go next.

Le Figaro Economie, 28 May · Capital, 29 May · France 2, *Journal de 13h*, 29 May ·
France 3, *19/20*, 29 May · LCI, 30 May · BFM Business, 30 May · Ouest-France, 30 May ·
Economie Matin, 31 May · Les Echos, "Restauration, logement, transport : les taux réduits de TVA
dans le viseur de Le Maire", 7 June · L'Express, "A qui profitent les TVA réduites visées par
Bercy ?", 11 June. Also Alternatives Économiques and Libération.
[IPP brief and press
list](https://www.ipp.eu/en/news/ipp-policy-brief-n32who-benefited-from-the-july-2009-sit-down-restaurant-value-added-tax-cuts/)

October 2018 ·

### Expert testimony

I served as expert witness for the Federal Trade Commission in *FTC v. H&R Block*, 2025, filing a
report and sitting for deposition.
[Case materials](https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/hr-block-matter)

### In government documents

The [Economic Report of the
President](https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/ERP_2018_Final-FINAL.pdf)
of February 2018 takes its estimate of American tax compliance costs from our work: "Benzarti
(2017) estimates that the total cost of filing all schedules of the Federal income tax increased
from $150 billion in 1984 to $200 billion in 2006 (1.4 percent of 2006 GDP)."

The Österreichische Energieagentur applied the asymmetry to Austria's solar-PV VAT exemption for
the climate and energy ministry in ["Photovoltaikpreise im
Sinkflug"](https://www.bmwet.gv.at/dam/jcr:51094b61-b47e-43e6-a5f3-f4947f2ef8b5/PV_Marktbeobachtung_Factsheet_2024.pdf),
November 2024.
